target.title: fix(sessions): prevent delivery-mirror prompt contamination with adjacent dedup and identity fallback (#99470)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a delivery-mirror assistant entry gets stripped of its `provider`/`model` metadata during session rebuild or side-branch merge, it survives the transcript-only filter and leaks into the model prompt as a duplicate assistant message. This causes prompt contamination where the model sees its own prior output twice — once from the real reply and once from the stripped delivery-mirror receipt.

Fixes #99470.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Layer 1 — Identity fallback**: `isTranscriptOnlyOpenClawAssistantMessage` on main only checks `role`, `provider`, and `model`. When session rebuild/side-branch merge strips `provider`/`model` from a delivery-mirror entry, the entry becomes invisible to this predicate and survives into replay. Adding an `openclawDeliveryMirror` field check catches these stripped-metadata survivors.

**Layer 2 — Adjacent dedup**: Even with Layer 1, implicit-channel receipts that mirror the assistant reply byte-for-byte can still appear adjacent to the real reply in the normalized transcript. `normalizeAssistantReplayContent` now collapses adjacent byte-identical assistant messages when neither carries tool calls.

**P1 fix — Native tool_use detection**: In `extractToolCallsFromAssistant()` (`tool-call-id.ts`), the `TOOL_CALL_TYPES` set recognizes `"toolCall"`, `"toolUse"`, and `"functionCall"` but not `"tool_use"` — the native Anthropic API content block type. When `isAdjacentAssistantDuplicate()` calls this helper to guard against collapsing tool-call-bearing turns, native `tool_use` blocks are invisible to the guard. An assistant turn carrying `{ type: "tool_use", id: "toolu_001", name: "read" }` appears to have zero tool calls, so if its text content matches a preceding delivery-mirror receipt it is collapsed as a duplicate. Only camelCase `"toolUse"` blocks had this protection; `"tool_use"` blocks — emitted by the Anthropic transport stream and handled by many other codepaths in the codebase — lacked it and could be silently dropped.

**Not modified**: Session persistence logic, gateway message broadcast, user-visible transcript display.

## User Impact

Users running agents with delivery-mirror channels no longer experience prompt contamination where duplicate assistant messages inflate token usage and degrade model output quality. Tool-call-bearing assistant turns are preserved regardless of whether the tool call uses camelCase (`toolUse`) or snake_case (`tool_use`) content blocks.

## Evidence

**Behavior addressed**: Delivery-mirror assistant entries leak into model prompt as duplicate messages after session rebuild or side-branch merge

**Real environment tested**: `node --import tsx`, local Node.js runtime, no external credentials required

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `node --import tsx scripts/repro/issue-99470-proof.mts`

**Evidence after fix**:
```
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Case 1 — openclawDeliveryMirror identity fallback
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Stripped mirror entry:
  provider: <undefined>
  model: <undefined>
  openclawDeliveryMirror: { kind: 'channel-final' }
  isTranscriptOnly: true          ← Layer 1 catches stripped-metadata survivor

Normal assistant (no delivery-mirror marker):
  isTranscriptOnly: false         ← real reply correctly survives filter
  ✓ PASS

Case 2 — Adjacent byte-identical duplicate collapse
  Input: 4 messages (user, assistant, stripped-mirror-duplicate, user)
  Output: 3 messages               ← duplicate collapsed, model sees 1 reply
  ✓ PASS

Case 3 — Both layers: identity fallback + adjacent dedup
  Input: 6 messages
  Output: 3 messages               ← both layers work together in single pass
  ✓ PASS

Case 4 — Native tool_use blocks prevent collapse (P1 fix)
  Input: 3 messages (user, native-tool_use-turn, text-only-dup)
  Output: 3 messages               ← tool_use turn preserved, not collapsed
  ✓ PASS

Case 5 — Native tool_use in both prev and next prevents collapse
  Input: 3 messages (user, tool_use-turn-a, tool_use-turn-b)
  Output: 3 messages               ← both tool_use turns survive
  ✓ PASS

5/5 proof cases passed
✓ ALL PROOF CASES PASSED
```

**Observed result after fix**: All 5 proof cases pass. Stripped-metadata delivery-mirror entries are correctly identified as transcript-only (Case 1). Adjacent byte-identical duplicates are collapsed (Cases 2-3). Native `tool_use` blocks prevent collapse of tool-call-bearing turns — before fix, Case 4's native `tool_use` turn was treated as having zero tool calls by the old guard so when its text matched a delivery-mirror duplicate it was silently collapsed, dropping native tool_use blocks and risking orphan tool_results in the provider prompt. After fix, tool_use-bearing turns are preserved (Cases 4-5).

**What was not tested**: External provider API integration, gateway message broadcast paths, session persistence to disk, side-branch merge on a live running gateway.

## Regression Test Plan

```
$ npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  37 passed (37)

$ npx vitest run src/agents/tool-call-id.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  26 passed (26)

$ npx vitest run src/agents/sessions/session-manager.test.ts --run
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  96 passed (96)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/tool-call-id.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts \
    src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.test.ts \
    src/shared/transcript-only-openclaw-assistant.ts
→ exit 0
```

## AI Assistance

This PR was created with assistance from Claude Opus 4.8 (Anthropic). The author understands and takes responsibility for all code changes. Key prompts included generating the native `tool_use` detection fix and the multi-layer proof script design.
